title: Quantum Geometry and Topology of Bulk Plasmons in Weyl Metals
authors: Hong-Yi Xie, Peter Abbamonte, Bruno Uchoa
abstract: We address the quantum geometric structure of plasmons in Fermi surfaces enclosing a topological charge. We demonstrate that Weyl fermion plasmons have monopole structure, are topological and have a finite vorticity $ζ=2\mathsf{C}_{\text{w}}$, where $\mathsf{C}_{\text{w}}$ is the Chern number of the Fermi surface enclosing the Weyl point. We show that these plasmons selectively couple to light linearly polarized along the plasmon effective dipole moment $\mathbf{d}$, which has quantum geometric origin and points along the direction of the plasmon center of mass momentum $\hat{\mathbf{Q}}$. We suggest that Weyl metal topological plasmons have distinctive optical properties compared to conventional plasmons.
summary: This theoretical work investigates how the topology inherent in Weyl metals dictates the nature of their collective plasmon excitations. It proves that these plasmons carry a topological charge quantified by vorticity ($\zeta$), which manifests as unique optical selection rules, allowing them to interact preferentially with light polarized along specific directions.
main_problem: The study addresses the quantum geometric structure and topological properties of plasmons—collective excitations—within Weyl metals.
main_result: Weyl metal plasmons are shown to possess a monopole structure and finite vorticity ($\zeta = 2C_W$), leading to unique optical selection rules where they couple selectively to light polarized along the dipole moment $\mathbf{d}$.
method: The analysis employs linear response theory (RPA) applied to the electron-hole pair operators, utilizing concepts from Berry curvature and quantum geometry tensors.
model_or_system: The system is Weyl metals, modeled by a Hamiltonian describing fermionic spinors. The physics is analyzed through the plasmon polarization bubble $\Pi_R(Q, \omega)$ and its susceptibility tensor $\chi_{ij}(\omega)$.
key_observables: Plasmon dispersion ($\omega_Q$), vorticity ($\zeta$), effective dipole moment ($\mathbf{d}$), and optical selection rules for light coupling.
important_parameters: Fermi momentum ($k_F$), plasmon frequency ($\omega_0$), and the topological charge (Chern number $C_W$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the Random Phase Approximation (RPA) level for plasmon calculation, assuming weak light fields and zero temperature in some derivations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the monopole structure of interband components, showing nodal planes ($\zeta=0$) and vortex structures ($\zeta=\pm 2$) related to different plasmon components.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the quantum geometric framework using form factor matrices to calculating the polarization function $\Pi_R$ via integrals. It then analyzes the resulting susceptibility tensor $\chi_{ij}(\omega)$ to derive unique optical selection rules and predict phenomena like Second Harmonic Generation (SHG).
why_interesting: The connection between topological invariants (Chern number) and measurable optical properties (polarization selection rules, SHG) is highly relevant for quantum optics and condensed matter theory.
